availability_source: JustWatch US (apis.justwatch.com), subscription (flatrate) offers only, checked 2026-10-25

items.title: Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse
items.why: Sequel to your 11. Same team, same art style, same wit. Note: part 1 of 2, ends on a cliffhanger.
items.synopsis: After reuniting with Gwen Stacy, Brooklyn’s full-time, friendly neighborhood Spider-Man is catapulted across the Multiverse, where he encounters the Spider Society, a team of Spider-People charged with protecting the Multiverse's very existence. But when the heroes clash on how to handle a new threat, Miles finds himself pitted against the other Spiders and must set out on his own to save those he loves most.

items.title: Weapons
items.why: Mystery-box horror from the Barbarian director: a whole class vanishes at 2:17 a.m. Told in puzzle-piece chapters, no filler.
items.synopsis: When all but one child from the same class mysteriously vanish on the same night at exactly the same time, a community is left questioning who or what is behind their disappearance.

items.title: Companion
items.why: Sci-fi dark comedy thriller with Black Mirror energy. A weekend getaway with a twist that keeps escalating.
items.synopsis: During a weekend getaway at a secluded lakeside estate, a group of friends finds themselves entangled in a web of secrets, deception, and advanced technology. As tensions rise and loyalties are tested, they uncover unsettling truths about themselves and the world around them.

items.title: Final Destination Bloodlines
items.why: Rule-based death traps (you gave FD an 8.6). Fresh lore, inventive kills, and a fast pace.
items.synopsis: Plagued by a violent recurring nightmare, college student Stefanie heads home to track down the one person who might be able to break the cycle and save her family from the grisly demise that inevitably awaits them all.

items.title: Memento
items.why: Nolan's rule-based puzzle, told backwards (Inception 10, The Prestige 9).
items.synopsis: Leonard Shelby is tracking down the man who raped and murdered his wife. The difficulty of locating his wife's killer, however, is compounded by the fact that he suffers from a rare, untreatable form of short-term memory loss. Although he can recall details of life before his accident, Leonard cannot remember what happened fifteen minutes ago, where he's going, or why.

items.title: Aliens
items.why: Prometheus 8.5 plus competent operators under siege. The franchise's action peak.
items.synopsis: Ripley, the sole survivor of the Nostromo's deadly encounter with the monstrous Alien, returns to Earth after drifting through space in hypersleep for 57 years. Although her story is initially met with skepticism, she agrees to accompany a team of Colonial Marines back to LV-426.

items.title: Ready or Not
items.why: Horror-comedy survival game with rules, in the Cabin in the Woods vein. Tight 95 minutes.
items.synopsis: A young bride's wedding night turns into her worst nightmare when her ridiculously rich in-laws force her to play a gruesome game of hide-and-seek.

items.title: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery
items.why: Twisty whodunit with satirical bite. Mystery plus the irreverent wit you score highly.
items.synopsis: World-famous detective Benoit Blanc heads to Greece to peel back the layers of a mystery surrounding a tech billionaire and his eclectic crew of friends.

items.title: Deadpool & Wolverine
items.why: You gave Deadpool 1 and 2 a 9 each. Irreverent superhero is your strongest superhero lane.
items.synopsis: A listless Wade Wilson toils away in civilian life with his days as the morally flexible mercenary, Deadpool, behind him. But when his homeworld faces an existential threat, Wade must reluctantly suit-up again with an even more reluctant Wolverine.

items.title: Snatch
items.why: Ensemble crime comedy with momentum, like Bullet Train 9.5 and Pulp Fiction.
items.synopsis: Unscrupulous boxing promoters, violent bookies, a Russian gangster, incompetent amateur robbers, and supposedly Jewish jewellers fight to track down a priceless stolen diamond.

items.title: Nightcrawler
items.why: Dark crime thriller with a magnetic, morally bankrupt lead (Ozark and Breaking Bad energy).
items.synopsis: When Lou Bloom, desperate for work, muscles into the world of L.A. crime journalism, he blurs the line between observer and participant to become the star of his own story. Aiding him in his effort is Nina, a TV-news veteran.

items.title: Coherence
items.why: A dinner party, a passing comet, and realities that start overlapping. Pure high-concept puzzle on a tiny budget, with a sharp final turn.
items.synopsis: Four couples gather for dinner the night a mysterious and powerful comet passes overhead.

items.title: Triangle
items.why: Time-loop horror at sea that plays like a Final Destination puzzle box. Every loop changes what you thought you saw.
items.synopsis: When Jess sets sail on a yacht with a group of friends, she cannot shake the feeling that there is something wrong.

items.title: The Thing
items.why: Paranoia in Antarctica: anyone could be the alien. It's the creature-feature peak your Prometheus and Aliens scores point to.
items.synopsis: A research team in Antarctica is hunted by a shape-shifting alien that assumes the appearance of its victims.

items.title: Alien
items.why: The original that Prometheus (8.5) and Aliens build on. Tighter and scarier than its reputation as a slow classic suggests.
items.synopsis: During its return to the earth, commercial spaceship Nostromo intercepts a distress signal from a distant planet. When a three-member team of the crew discovers a chamber containing thousands of eggs on the planet, a creature inside one of the eggs attacks an explorer. The entire crew is unaware of the impending nightmare set to descend upon them when the alien parasite planted inside its unfortunate host is birthed.

items.title: Talk to Me
items.why: Horror with a clear rule (the hand, 90 seconds, then let go) that the kids break. Close to The Ring (9) in rule-driven dread.
items.synopsis: When a group of friends discover how to conjure spirits using an embalmed hand, they become hooked on the new thrill, until one of them goes too far and unleashes terrifying supernatural forces.

items.title: Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery
items.why: Benoit Blanc's third case, an impossible-crime mystery. If Glass Onion is on your list, this is the next one.
items.synopsis: When young priest Jud Duplenticy is sent to assist charismatic firebrand Monsignor Jefferson Wicks, it’s clear that all is not well in the pews. After a sudden and seemingly impossible murder rocks the town, the lack of an obvious suspect prompts local police chief Geraldine Scott to join forces with renowned detective Benoit Blanc to unravel a mystery that defies all logic.

items.title: Sinners
items.why: A 1930s juke-joint night turns into a vampire siege. Crime and horror, with a big crowd-pleasing final hour.
items.synopsis: Trying to leave their troubled lives behind, twin brothers return to their hometown to start again, only to discover that an even greater evil is waiting to welcome them back.

items.title: Final Destination 5
items.why: The best sequel: the bridge collapse is the franchise's top kill set piece, and the ending ties into the first film (8.6).
items.synopsis: Death is just as omnipresent as ever, and is unleashed after one man’s premonition saves a group of coworkers from a terrifying suspension bridge collapse. But this group of unsuspecting souls was never supposed to survive, and, in a terrifying race against time, the ill-fated group frantically tries to discover a way to escape Death’s sinister agenda.

items.title: Saw X
items.why: Jigsaw back in full puzzle-trap mode. The best-reviewed Saw since your 8.7 original.
items.synopsis: A sick and desperate John travels to Mexico for a risky and experimental medical procedure in hopes of a miracle cure for his cancer only to discover the entire operation is a scam to defraud the most vulnerable.

items.title: Godzilla Minus One
items.why: Kaiju movie with real stakes and a clever engineering-plan finale. Not filler, and one of the best-reviewed of the decade.
items.synopsis: In postwar Japan, Godzilla brings new devastation to an already scorched landscape. With no military intervention or government help in sight, the survivors must join together in the face of despair and fight back against an unrelenting horror.

items.title: Nope
items.why: A high-concept UFO mystery with an original rule for how the thing hunts. Builds to a smart, spectacular last act.
items.synopsis: Residents in a lonely gulch of inland California bear witness to an uncanny, chilling discovery.

items.title: Bodies Bodies Bodies
items.why: A party whodunit where the Gen Z guests turn on each other. Short, nasty, and the ending is a great punchline.
items.synopsis: In an isolated family mansion, a group of rich 20-somethings decides to play Bodies Bodies Bodies, a game where one of them is secretly a "killer" while the rest tries to "escape". Things take a turn for the worse when real bodies start turning up, setting off a paranoid and dangerous chain of events.

items.title: Alien: Romulus
items.why: Back to Aliens-style horror: young scavengers on a derelict station full of facehuggers. Fast, practical effects, and it ties into Prometheus (8.5).
items.synopsis: While scavenging the deep ends of a derelict space station, a group of young space colonists come face to face with the most terrifying life form in the universe.

items.title: Barbarian
items.why: An Airbnb double-booking becomes a horror movie that keeps changing genre. Wild twists, nothing slow.
items.synopsis: In town for a job interview, a young woman arrives at her Airbnb late at night only to find that it has been mistakenly double-booked and a strange man is already staying there. Against her better judgement, she decides to stay the night anyway.

items.title: Boss Level
items.why: An action time loop: an ex-soldier relives the day assassins kill him. Edge of Tomorrow (9) meets John Wick (10).
items.synopsis: A former special forces agent is trapped in a time loop and relives his death over and over again. To escape the terrible situation, he must track down those responsible and stop them.

items.title: Palm Springs
items.why: Time-loop dark comedy at a wedding. Sharper and stranger than Groundhog Day, with clever loop rules.
items.synopsis: When carefree Nyles and reluctant maid of honor Sarah have a chance encounter at a Palm Springs wedding, things get complicated when they find themselves unable to escape the venue, themselves, or each other.

items.title: The Substance
items.why: A high-concept body-horror satire: a drug that makes a 'better you', with one strict rule. A gonzo ending.
items.synopsis: A fading celebrity takes a black-market drug: a cell-replicating substance that helps her create a younger, better version of herself.

items.title: Heretic
items.why: Two missionaries knock on the wrong door. A battle-of-wits horror built on puzzles and reversals.
items.synopsis: Two young Mormon women are drawn into a game of cat-and-mouse in the house of a strange man.

items.title: No One Will Save You
items.why: Home-invasion alien horror with almost no dialogue, but it moves. Tense set pieces and an inventive creature design.
items.synopsis: An exiled anxiety-ridden homebody must battle an alien who's found its way into her home.

items.title: Predator: Killer of Killers
items.why: An animated Predator anthology: a Viking, a samurai, and a WWII pilot each face a hunter. Love, Death & Robots (10) energy.
items.synopsis: While three of the fiercest warriors in human history—a Viking raider, a ninja in feudal Japan, and a WWII pilot—are killers in their own right, they are merely prey for their new opponent: the ultimate killer of killers.

items.title: Predator: Badlands
items.why: A Predator flips the franchise: a young Yautja hunts on a death planet with a synthetic ally. Big creature action.
items.synopsis: Cast out from his clan, a young Predator finds an unlikely ally in a damaged android and embarks on a treacherous journey in search of the ultimate adversary.

items.title: Self Reliance
items.why: A dark comedy with a high-concept game show: survive 30 days while hunters try to kill him, but he's safe if he's with another person.
items.synopsis: When a man is offered a million dollars to play a game in which hunters try to kill him, he thinks he has found the perfect loophole: they can only attack when he’s alone. His only problem is that none of his friends or family believe the game is real. Forced to seek companionship in unexpected places, he navigates the bizarre challenge with humor, paranoia, and a surprising search for connection.

items.title: Rebel Ridge
items.why: A tense, grounded action thriller: an ex-Marine against a corrupt small-town police force. Smart escalation, no camp.
items.synopsis: A former Marine confronts corruption in a small town when local law enforcement unjustly seizes the bag of cash he needs to post his cousin's bail.

items.title: Sicario
items.why: A cartel-war thriller with one of the great tension set pieces (the border crossing). Serious, brutal, and fast.
items.synopsis: An idealistic FBI agent is enlisted by a government task force to aid in the escalating war against drugs at the border area between the U.S. and Mexico.

items.title: Final Destination 2
items.why: The log-truck highway pileup is the series' most famous opening. Pure Final Destination (8.6) rules.
items.synopsis: When Kimberly has a violent premonition of a highway pileup she blocks the freeway, keeping a few others meant to die, safe...Or are they? The survivors mysteriously start dying and it's up to Kimberly to stop it before she's next.

items.title: Oblivion
items.why: A drone repairman on a ruined Earth learns his mission is a lie. Big-concept sci-fi with a satisfying twist.
items.synopsis: Jack Harper is one of the last few drone repairmen stationed on Earth. Part of a massive operation to extract vital resources after decades of war with a terrifying threat known as the Scavs, Jack’s mission is nearly complete. His existence is brought crashing down when he rescues a beautiful  stranger from a downed spacecraft. Her arrival triggers a chain of events that  forces him to question everything he knows and puts the fate of humanity in his hands.

items.title: Us
items.why: Peele's high-concept doppelganger horror, with a reveal that reframes it. More of a rules-and-twist film than Get Out (8).
items.synopsis: Husband and wife Gabe and Adelaide Wilson take their kids to their beach house expecting to unplug and unwind with friends. But as night descends, their serenity turns to tension and chaos when some shocking visitors arrive uninvited.

items.title: Sunshine
items.why: A crew flying a bomb to reignite the sun. Sci-fi thriller that turns into horror in the last act, with Event Horizon energy.
items.synopsis: Fifty years into the future, the sun is dying, and Earth is threatened by arctic temperatures. A team of astronauts is sent to revive the Sun — but the mission fails. Seven years later, a new team is sent to finish the mission as mankind’s last hope.

items.title: The Ritual
items.why: Friends take a shortcut through a Swedish forest and something hunts them. A creature reveal that really pays off.
items.synopsis: A group of college friends reunite for a trip to the forest, but encounter a menacing presence in the woods that's stalking them.

items.title: Green Room
items.why: A punk band trapped in a neo-Nazi club after witnessing a murder. A siege thriller that's lean, vicious, and short.
items.synopsis: Members of a punk rock band and a tough young woman are forced to fight for survival after witnessing an act of violence at a skinhead bar.

items.title: Wrath of Man
items.why: Guy Ritchie's darker crime revenge thriller, told out of order like a heist puzzle. Jason Statham at his coldest.
items.synopsis: A cold and mysterious new security guard for a Los Angeles cash truck company surprises his co-workers when he unleashes precision skills during a heist. The crew is left wondering who he is and where he came from. Soon, the marksman's ultimate motive becomes clear as he takes dramatic and irrevocable steps to settle a score.

items.title: Heat
items.why: The crime-epic gold standard: a master thief and the detective who matches him. The downtown shootout alone is worth it.
items.synopsis: Obsessive master thief Neil McCauley leads a top-notch crew on various daring heists throughout Los Angeles while determined detective Vincent Hanna pursues him without rest. Each man recognizes and respects the ability and the dedication of the other even though they are aware their cat-and-mouse game may end in violence.

items.title: The Departed
items.why: Two moles, one in the mob and one in the police, hunt each other. A twisty crime thriller with a famous ending.
items.synopsis: To take down South Boston's Irish Mafia, the police send in one of their own to infiltrate the underworld, not realizing the syndicate has done likewise. While an undercover cop curries favor with the mob kingpin, a career criminal rises through the police ranks. But both sides soon discover there's a mole among them.

items.title: Trap
items.why: Shyamalan: a serial killer realizes the concert he's at is a police trap. The Village (9) director in playful cat-and-mouse mode.
items.synopsis: A father and teen daughter attend a pop concert, where they realize they're at the center of a dark and sinister event.

items.title: Knock at the Cabin
items.why: Shyamalan's high-concept apocalypse dilemma: four strangers demand a sacrifice. Tight at 100 minutes.
items.synopsis: A vacationing family is terrorized by four strangers, who alternately claim to be either averting, or bringing about, the apocalypse.

items.title: The Accountant 2
items.why: A sequel to The Accountant (8.9) you rated highly: the autistic forensic accountant plus his brother, with more action and humor.
items.synopsis: When an old acquaintance is murdered, Wolff is compelled to solve the case. Realizing more extreme measures are necessary, Wolff recruits his estranged and highly lethal brother, Brax, to help. In partnership with Marybeth Medina, they uncover a deadly conspiracy, becoming targets of a ruthless network of killers who will stop at nothing to keep their secrets buried.

items.title: Sinister
items.why: Found home movies hide a supernatural killer. The closest modern match to The Ring (9).
items.synopsis: True-crime writer Ellison Oswalt is in a slump; he hasn't had a best seller in more than 10 years and is becoming increasingly desperate for a hit. So, when he discovers the existence of a snuff film showing the deaths of a family, he vows to solve the mystery. He moves his own family into the victims' home and gets to work. However, when old film footage and other clues hint at the presence of a supernatural force, Ellison learns that living in the house may be fatal.

items.title: The Black Phone
items.why: A kidnapped boy gets calls from the killer's dead victims on a disconnected phone. A clear supernatural rule and a tense escape.
items.synopsis: Finney Blake, a shy but clever 13-year-old boy, is abducted by a sadistic killer and trapped in a soundproof basement where screaming is of little use. When a disconnected phone on the wall begins to ring, Finney discovers that he can hear the voices of the killer’s previous victims. And they are dead set on making sure that what happened to them doesn’t happen to Finney.

items.title: Thunderbolts*
items.why: Marvel's misfit-antiheroes team-up, closer to The Suicide Squad (9) than standard MCU. Darker and funnier.
items.synopsis: After finding themselves ensnared in a death trap, an unconventional team of antiheroes must go on a dangerous mission that will force them to confront the darkest corners of their pasts.

items.title: Invincible
items.why: The Boys (10) as Western adult animation: brutal, funny, and long-arc.
items.synopsis: Mark Grayson is a normal teenager except for the fact that his father is the most powerful superhero on the planet. Shortly after his seventeenth birthday, Mark begins to develop powers of his own and enters into his father's tutelage.

items.title: Pantheon
items.why: Mind-upload sci-fi with Black Mirror and Altered Carbon stakes. Complete in 2 seasons.
items.synopsis: A bullied teen receives mysterious help from someone online: a stranger soon revealed to be her recently deceased father, David, whose consciousness has been uploaded to the Cloud following an experimental destructive brain scan. David is the first of a new kind of being – an “Uploaded Intelligence” or “UI” – but he will not be the last, as a global conspiracy unfolds that threatens to trigger a new kind of world war.

items.title: Peacemaker
items.why: James Gunn's irreverent superhero comedy (The Suicide Squad 9).
items.synopsis: The continuing story of Peacemaker, a vainglorious superhero/supervillain who believes in peace at any cost — no matter how many people he has to kill. After a miraculous recovery from his duel with Bloodsport, Peacemaker soon discovers that his freedom comes at a price.

items.title: The Expanse
items.why: Rule-consistent hard sci-fi with a big mystery. Complete in 6 seasons. S1 starts slow, then takes off.
items.synopsis: A thriller set two hundred years in the future following the case of a missing young woman who brings a hardened detective and a rogue ship's captain together in a race across the solar system to expose the greatest conspiracy in human history.

items.title: Gen V
items.why: Spin-off of The Boys: same tone, same universe, shorter seasons.
items.synopsis: At America's only college for superheroes, gifted students put their moral boundaries to the test, competing for the university's top ranking, and a chance to join The Seven, Vought International's elite superhero team. When the school's dark secrets come to light, they must decide what kind of heroes they want to become.

items.title: From
items.why: Mystery-box horror: a town nobody can leave and monsters with rules. Lost meets Dark.
items.synopsis: Unravel the mystery of a nightmarish town in middle America that traps all those who enter. As the unwilling residents fight to keep a sense of normalcy and search for a way out, they must also survive the threats of the surrounding forest – including the terrifying creatures that come out when the sun goes down.

items.title: Barry
items.why: Hitman dark comedy about a competent killer who wants out (Ozark, Dexter).
items.synopsis: A hit man from the Midwest moves to Los Angeles and gets caught up in the city's theatre arts scene.

items.title: Harley Quinn
items.why: Archer-style adult animated action comedy with a strong cast and a fast pace.
items.synopsis: Harley Quinn has finally broken things off once and for all with the Joker. Now, she's trying to make it on her own as the criminal Queenpin of Gotham City, with help from Poison Ivy and a ragtag crew of DC castoffs.

items.title: Creature Commandos
items.why: Gunn's adult-animated monster squad. Irreverent superhero action in 7 episodes.
items.synopsis: A group of nonhuman criminals comprised of an anthropomorphic weasel, a robot, the bride of Frankenstein, a radioactive skeleton, and their human leader are tasked with stopping an evil sorceress.

items.title: Castlevania: Nocturne
items.why: Follow-up to Castlevania (your 9). Dark fantasy action, set during the French Revolution.
items.synopsis: As revolution sweeps France, Richter Belmont fights to uphold his family's legacy and prevent the rise of a ruthless, power-hungry vampire ruler.

items.title: IT: Welcome to Derry
items.why: Big-budget horror prequel built on Pennywise's rules and history.
items.synopsis: In 1962, amid a spate of unexplained disappearances of local children, a group of misfit friends begin to suspect a long-buried ancient evil lurking. As the kids set out to determine what's really going on, a rising unease prompts several townspeople to work together to restore peace – all while a U.S. military operation seeks to exploit Derry for its own objectives.

items.title: The Penguin
items.why: Crime saga with a morally gray rise-to-power arc, like Ozark and Breaking Bad.
items.synopsis: Follow Oswald "Oz" Cobb’s quest for control as he seeks to fill the power vacuum left by the death of Carmine Falcone, transforming from a disfigured nobody to a noted mobster in Gotham City.

items.title: Travelers
items.why: Future operatives' minds are sent into people about to die, to stop a collapse. Time-travel rules with Dark-style consequences, complete in 3 seasons.
items.synopsis: Hundreds of years from now, the last surviving humans discover the means of sending consciousness back through time, directly into people in the 21st century. These "travelers" assume the lives of seemingly random people, while secretly working as teams to perform missions in order to save humanity from a terrible future.

items.title: Fringe
items.why: High-concept X-Files with parallel universes, built on a big mythology that pays off. It finishes on a real ending.
items.synopsis: An F.B.I. agent is forced to work with an institutionalized scientist and his son in order to rationalize a brewing storm of unexplained phenomena.

items.title: Person of Interest
items.why: An AI predicts crimes and two men act on its numbers. It turns into a superintelligence war, and it ends well.
items.synopsis: John Reese, former CIA paramilitary operative, is presumed dead and teams up with reclusive billionaire Finch to prevent violent crimes in New York City by initiating their own type of justice. With the special training that Reese has had in Covert Operations and Finch's genius software inventing mind, the two are a perfect match for the job that they have to complete. With the help of surveillance equipment, they work "outside the law" and get the right criminal behind bars.

items.title: Hannibal
items.why: A crime procedural that's really a horror series, with a stunning cat-and-mouse. For your Se7en and Bates Motel (9) side.
items.synopsis: Explores the early relationship between renowned psychiatrist Hannibal Lecter and a young FBI criminal profiler who is haunted by his ability to empathize with serial killers.

items.title: The Boys Presents: Diabolical
items.why: An animated The Boys (10) anthology in Love, Death & Robots (10) form: short, savage, and wildly varied.
items.synopsis: A collection of animated short stories that takes place inside The Boys (2019) universe.

items.title: Guillermo del Toro's Cabinet of Curiosities
items.why: Horror anthology with a new director every episode. Black Mirror-style self-contained stories, mostly Lovecraftian.
items.synopsis: Bizarre nightmares unfold in eight tales of terror in this visually stunning, spine-tingling horror collection curated by Guillermo del Toro.

items.title: The Legend of Vox Machina
items.why: Adult animated fantasy: a D&D party with Archer-level crude humor and real stakes, dragons included.
items.synopsis: After saving the realm from evil and destruction at the hands of the most terrifying power couple in Exandria, Vox Machina is faced with saving the world once again-this time, from a sinister group of dragons known as the Chroma Conclave.

items.title: Blue Eye Samurai
items.why: A revenge epic in Edo Japan with stunning animation. Its action-and-plot balance is like Castlevania (9).
items.synopsis: In Edo-period Japan, a young warrior driven by a dream of revenge cuts a bloody path toward destiny.

items.title: Common Side Effects
items.why: Adult Swim dark comedy thriller: a mushroom that cures everything, and the pharma and government agents hunting it.
items.synopsis: Former high school lab partners Marshall and Frances begin to unravel a conspiracy involving big pharma and the federal government to suppress knowledge of a rare mushroom that may hold the key to curing all the world’s diseases.

items.title: True Detective
items.why: Season 1 is an occult-tinged serial-killer case told across two timelines. Standalone, so you can stop after it.
items.synopsis: An American anthology police detective series utilizing multiple timelines in which investigations seem to unearth personal and professional secrets of those involved, both within or outside the law.

items.title: The Gentlemen
items.why: Guy Ritchie crime comedy, the series. An aristocrat inherits an estate with a weed empire under it. Snatch energy.
items.synopsis: When aristocratic Eddie inherits the family estate, he discovers that it's home to a huge weed empire, and its proprietors aren't going anywhere.

items.title: Loki
items.why: The MCU's best show is a time-bureaucracy heist. Season 2's finale is a real ending.
items.synopsis: The mercurial villain Loki resumes his role as the God of Mischief in a new series that takes place after the events of “Avengers: Endgame.”

items.title: The Sandman
items.why: Dream-king fantasy from Neil Gaiman, made of distinct arcs. Includes a standout horror diner episode.
items.synopsis: After years of imprisonment, Morpheus — the King of Dreams — embarks on a journey across worlds to find what was stolen from him and restore his power.

items.title: Russian Doll
items.why: A dark comedy time loop: she dies every night at her 36th birthday party. Tight, 8 episodes.
items.synopsis: Nadia keeps dying and reliving her 36th birthday party. She's trapped in a surreal time loop -- and staring down the barrel of her own mortality.

items.title: The Outsider
items.why: Stephen King: an impossible crime with the suspect in two places at once. Procedural that slides into supernatural.
items.synopsis: When an insidious supernatural force edges its way into a seemingly straightforward investigation into the gruesome murder of a young boy, it leads a seasoned cop and an unorthodox investigator to question everything they believe in.

items.title: X-Men '97
items.why: A revival of the 90s cartoon that's genuinely great. Big twists, and escalating like a superhero Game of Thrones.
items.synopsis: The X-Men, a band of mutants who use their uncanny gifts to protect a world that hates and fears them, are challenged like never before, forced to face a dangerous and unexpected new future.

items.title: Orphan Black
items.why: Clone conspiracy thriller with a lead playing a dozen characters. Fast-moving and high-concept, and it ends well.
items.synopsis: A streetwise hustler is pulled into a compelling conspiracy after witnessing the suicide of a girl who looks just like her.

items.title: Kingdom
items.why: A Joseon-era zombie political thriller: palace intrigue plus a plague. Two tight seasons.
items.synopsis: In this zombie thriller set in Korea's medieval Joseon dynasty which has been defeated by corruption and famine, a mysterious rumor of the king’s death spreads, as does a strange plague that renders the infected immune to death and hungry for flesh. The crown prince, fallen victim to a conspiracy, sets out on a journey to unveil the evil scheme and save his people.

items.title: Alien: Earth
items.why: Noah Hawley's Alien series: hybrids, xenomorphs, and corporate war on Earth. For your Prometheus side.
items.synopsis: When the mysterious deep space research vessel USCSS Maginot crash-lands on Earth, Wendy and a ragtag group of tactical soldiers make a fateful discovery that puts them face-to-face with the planet's greatest threat.

items.title: Fargo
items.why: Crime anthology with dark comedy and escalating violence. Each season is self-contained, with an Ozark (11) vibe.
items.synopsis: A close-knit anthology series dealing with stories involving malice, violence and murder based in and around Minnesota.

items.title: WandaVision
items.why: A high-concept sitcom mystery that unravels into a superhero reality-bender. 9 tight episodes. Currently streaming on Hulu.
items.synopsis: Wanda Maximoff and Vision—two super-powered beings living idealized suburban lives—begin to suspect that everything is not as it seems.

items.title: Lost
items.why: The original mystery-box show: a plane crash, an island, and a mythology that keeps escalating. The final season divides people, but the ride is huge.
items.synopsis: Stripped of everything, the survivors of a horrific plane crash  must work together to stay alive. But the island holds many secrets.

items.title: Paradise
items.why: A president is murdered, and a Secret Service agent investigates. The episode 1 twist reframes everything. Thriller pacing.
items.synopsis: The tranquility in a serene, wealthy community inhabited by some of the world's most prominent individuals explodes when a shocking murder occurs and a high stakes investigation unfolds.

items.title: Legion
items.why: Trippy X-Men-adjacent show about a mutant who may be insane. Inventive and high-concept, with 3 seasons and a full ending.
items.synopsis: David Haller, AKA Legion, is a troubled young man who may be more than human. Diagnosed as schizophrenic, David has been in and out of psychiatric hospitals for years. But after a strange encounter with a fellow patient, he’s confronted with the possibility that the voices he hears and the visions he sees might be real.

items.title: Castle Rock
items.why: A Stephen King multiverse mystery in a cursed town. Season 1 is a self-contained puzzle.
items.synopsis: Based on the stories of Stephen King, the series intertwines characters and themes from the fictional town of Castle Rock.

items.title: Hit-Monkey
items.why: Adult animated Marvel: a monkey assassin and the ghost of a hitman in Tokyo. Archer (11) energy with real violence.
items.synopsis: After a high-profile political assassination goes sideways, an injured hitman hides out amongst a tribe of snow monkeys in the mountains of Japan.

items.title: The Patient
items.why: A therapist chained in a serial killer's basement. 10 short, tense episodes with a firm ending.
items.synopsis: A psychotherapist finds himself held prisoner by a serial killer who demands he help him curb his homicidal urges.

items.title: Justified
items.why: A cowboy US Marshal in Kentucky crime country. Sharp dialogue and great villains, and it sticks the landing.
items.synopsis: A character drama based on the 2001 Elmore Leonard short story "Fire in the Hole." Leonard's tale centers around U.S. Marshal Raylan Givens of Kentucky, a quiet but strong-willed official of the law. The tale covers his high-stakes job, as well as his strained relationships with his ex-wife and father.

items.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power
items.why: Middle-earth's Second Age: Sauron's rise and the forging of the rings. Uneven, but huge for a Fellowship (12) fan, and season 2 is darker and better.
items.synopsis: Beginning in a time of relative peace, we follow an ensemble cast of characters as they confront the re-emergence of evil to Middle-earth. From the darkest depths of the Misty Mountains, to the majestic forests of Lindon, to the breathtaking island kingdom of Númenor, to the furthest reaches of the map, these kingdoms and characters will carve out legacies that live on long after they are gone.

items.title: Good Omens
items.why: An angel and a demon try to stop the apocalypse. Gaiman and Pratchett dark-comedy fantasy, Futurama-level wit.
items.synopsis: Aziraphale and Crowley, of Heaven and Hell respectively, have grown rather fond of the Earth. So it's terrible news that it's about to end. The armies of Good and Evil are amassing. The Four Horsemen are ready to ride. Everything is going according to the Divine Plan...except that someone seems to have misplaced the Antichrist. Can our heroes find him and stop Armageddon before it's too late?

items.title: Snowpiercer
items.why: The last humans on a perpetually moving train, with class war and murder mystery. High concept, complete in 4 seasons.
items.synopsis: More than seven years after the world has become a frozen wasteland, the remnants of humanity inhabit a gigantic, perpetually-moving train that circles the globe as class warfare, social injustice and the politics of survival play out.

items.title: Hazbin Hotel
items.why: Adult animated hell musical comedy: a princess of Hell tries to rehabilitate sinners. Crude, fast, and very Harley Quinn-adjacent.
items.synopsis: In attempt to find a non-violent alternative for reducing Hell's overpopulation, the daughter of Lucifer opens a rehabilitation hotel that offers a group of misfit demons a chance at redemption.

items.title: Mare of Easttown
items.why: A small-town detective and a murder with many suspects. A 7-episode mystery with a genuinely surprising, earned ending.
items.synopsis: A detective in a small Pennsylvania town investigates a local murder while trying to keep her life from falling apart.

items.title: All of Us Are Dead
items.why: A zombie outbreak traps students in a Korean high school. Relentless survival with real stakes.
items.synopsis: A high school becomes ground zero for a zombie virus outbreak. Trapped students must fight their way out — or turn into one of the rabid infected.

items.title: Parasyte: The Grey
items.why: Parasitic aliens take over human hosts in Korea, from the Train to Busan director. Six tight episodes of body horror action.
items.synopsis: When unidentified parasites violently take over human hosts and gain power, humanity must rise to combat the growing threat.

items.title: His Dark Materials
items.why: Fantasy across parallel worlds: daemons, armored bears, and a war on the Church. Complete and builds well.
items.synopsis: Lyra is an orphan who lives in a parallel universe in which science, theology and magic are entwined. Her search for a kidnapped friend uncovers a sinister plot involving stolen children and turns into a quest to understand a mysterious phenomenon called Dust. She is later joined on her journey by Will, a boy who possesses a knife that can cut windows between worlds. As she learns the truth about her parents and her prophesied destiny, the two young people are caught up in a war against celestial powers that ranges across many worlds.

items.title: The Strain
items.why: Del Toro's vampire plague hits New York: virology meets horror. Pulpy, gory, and fast once it gets going.
items.synopsis: A high concept thriller that tells the story of Dr. Ephraim Goodweather, the head of the Center for Disease Control Canary Team in New York City. He and his team are called upon to investigate a mysterious viral outbreak with hallmarks of an ancient and evil strain of vampirism. As the strain spreads, Eph, his team, and an assembly of everyday New Yorkers, wage war for the fate of humanity itself.

items.title: Cassandra
items.why: A German sci-fi horror miniseries: a family moves into a smart home whose 1970s AI won't let them go. Black Mirror (10) meets Dark (10).
items.synopsis: A family moves into a vintage smart home and discovers that it's under the control of a virtual assistant — who will stop at nothing to keep them there.

items.title: Mob Psycho 100
items.why: From the creator of One-Punch Man: a psychic power system and stakes that escalate, closest in spirit to Hunter x Hunter. Complete in 3 seasons.
items.synopsis: Shigeo Kageyama, a.k.a. "Mob," is a boy who has trouble expressing himself, but who happens to be a powerful esper. Mob is determined to live a normal life and keeps his ESP suppressed, but when his emotions surge to a level of 100%, something terrible happens to him! As he's surrounded by false espers, evil spirits, and mysterious organizations, what will Mob think? What choices will he make?

items.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure
items.why: Stand battles are rule-based puzzles, like Nen fights. Every part is a new arc with a new cast, so there's no filler.
items.synopsis: Follow the intergenerational feud between the Joestar Family and various forces of evil, the most prominent of which is Dio Brando and his followers.

items.title: Delicious in Dungeon
items.why: A Frieren-style fantasy party: a dungeon with hard ecological rules and a clever, funny crew.
items.synopsis: Dungeons, dragons... and delicious monster stew!? Adventurers foray into a cursed buried kingdom to save their friend, cooking up a storm along the way.

items.title: Death Note
items.why: High-concept cat-and-mouse between two geniuses, with strict rules. The first half is all-time great.
items.synopsis: Light Yagami is an ace student with great prospects—and he’s bored out of his mind. But all that changes when he finds the Death Note, a notebook dropped by a rogue Shinigami death god. Any human whose name is written in the notebook dies, and Light has vowed to use the power of the Death Note to rid the world of evil. But will Light succeed in his noble goal, or will the Death Note turn him into the very thing he fights against?

items.title: Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion
items.why: A strategic mastermind with one rule-bound power, plus mecha war and constant reversals. Complete in 2 seasons.
items.synopsis: Japan has been invaded and conquered by the Britannian Empire. Japan is now known as Area 11 and its citizens known as Elevens. The Britannian Empire takes away Japan's autonomous power and imposes its rule through the use of Knightmares. The Empire's rule has never faltered, but cracks have begun to show...

items.title: Dan Da Dan
items.why: Fast sci-fi horror comedy with aliens versus ghosts. Wild, kinetic, and never slow.
items.synopsis: When Momo and Okarun's beliefs clash, they're thrown into a world of ghosts, aliens and awakened powers.

items.title: Pluto
items.why: Sci-fi murder mystery about who is killing the world's greatest robots. Prestige-level and only 8 episodes.
items.synopsis: When the world's seven most advanced robots and their human allies are murdered one by one, Inspector Gesicht soon discovers that he's also in danger.

items.title: Psycho-Pass
items.why: Cyberpunk crime procedural in a Minority Report-style precrime state. Season 1 is the one to watch.
items.synopsis: In the year 2113, people are given brain scans to determine how likely they are to commit a crime. Those who fail are apprehended, or even killed.

items.title: Sakamoto Days
items.why: A retired legendary hitman fights off a stream of assassins: John Wick energy with comedy.
items.synopsis: Once the greatest hitman of all, Taro Sakamoto retired in the name of love. But when his past catches up, he must fight to protect his beloved family.

items.title: Odd Taxi
items.why: Crime mystery with dark comedy. Every conversation is a clue, and it all pays off in 13 episodes.
items.synopsis: While working as a taxi driver on the hectic streets of Tokyo, a reticent walrus gets pulled into a mystery involving a missing teenage girl.

items.title: Re:ZERO
items.why: Isekai with a brutal rule: he respawns at checkpoints when he dies. Darker than SAO or Slime.
items.synopsis: After being suddenly transported to another world, Subaru Natsuki and his new female partner are brutally murdered. However, Subaru awakens to a familiar scene, meeting the same girl again. The day begins to mysteriously repeat itself.

items.title: Lazarus
items.why: Cowboy Bebop director's sci-fi action thriller: find the man behind a deadly drug in 30 days. 13 episodes.
items.synopsis: In 2052, a Nobel Prize-winning neuroscientist develops a drug called Hapna — a cure-all that has the unexpected side-effect of causing death three years later. In response to this threat, a special force of agents—nicknamed "Lazarus"— is assembled to take on the malevolent Skinner.

items.title: Steins;Gate
items.why: Time-travel sci-fi thriller with strict rules. Slow first few episodes, then it becomes one of anime's best, Dark-style.
items.synopsis: A group of friends have customized their microwave so that it can send text messages to the past. As they perform different experiments, an organization named SERN who has been doing their own research on time travel tracks them down and now the characters have to find a way to avoid being captured by them.

items.title: Vinland Saga
items.why: Viking revenge epic. Season 1 is relentless; it's for your Game of Thrones and Frieren side.
items.synopsis: For a thousand years, the Vikings have made quite a name and reputation for themselves as the strongest families with a thirst for violence. Thorfinn, the son of one of the Vikings' greatest warriors, spends his boyhood in a battlefield enhancing his skills in his adventure to redeem his most-desired revenge after his father was murdered.

items.title: The Promised Neverland
items.why: Orphanage kids discover the truth and plan an escape. Season 1 is a near-perfect strategy thriller. Skip season 2.
items.synopsis: Emma, Norman and Ray are the brightest kids at the Grace Field House orphanage. And under the care of the woman they refer to as “Mom,” all the kids have enjoyed a comfortable life. Good food, clean clothes and the perfect environment to learn—what more could an orphan ask for? One day, though, Emma and Norman uncover the dark truth of the outside world they are forbidden from seeing.

items.title: Erased
items.why: A man sent back to his childhood to stop a serial killer. A 12-episode mystery that feels like Dark meets Zodiac.
items.synopsis: Satoru Fujinuma is a struggling manga artist who has the ability to turn back time and prevent deaths. When his mother is killed he turns back time to solve the mystery, but ends up back in elementary school, just before the disappearance of his classmate Kayo.

items.title: Overlord
items.why: A gamer trapped as his MMO's undead overlord, played as the villain. Slime (9) energy, but much darker.
items.synopsis: In the year 2138, virtual reality gaming is booming. Yggdrasil, a popular online game is quietly shut down one day. However, one player named Momonga decides to not log out. Momonga is then transformed into the image of a skeleton as "the most powerful wizard." The world continues to change, with non-player characters (NPCs) beginning to feel emotion. Having no parents, friends, or place in society, this ordinary young man Momonga then strives to take over the new world the game has become.

items.title: Devilman Crybaby
items.why: Brutal, wild 10-episode demon horror from Masaaki Yuasa. Ends hard.
items.synopsis: With demons reawakened and humanity in turmoil, a sensitive demon-boy is led into a brutal, degenerate war against evil by his mysterious friend, Ryo.

items.title: One-Punch Man
items.why: A hero so strong that every fight ends in one punch. The superhero satire is like The Boys (10), and the season 1 action is elite.
items.synopsis: Saitama, a superhero who can defeat any foe with a single punch, battles boredom as he searches for a worthy opponent in a world plagued by monsters.

items.title: Cowboy Bebop
items.why: Space bounty hunters, jazz, and noir. Most episodes are self-contained, with a famous ending.
items.synopsis: In 2071, roughly fifty years after an accident with a hyperspace gateway made the Earth almost uninhabitable, humanity has colonized most of the rocky planets and moons of the Solar System. Amid a rising crime rate, the Inter Solar System Police (ISSP) set up a legalized contract system, in which registered bounty hunters, also referred to as "Cowboys", chase criminals and bring them in alive in return for a reward.

items.title: Trigun Stampede
items.why: A CG reboot of the classic gunslinger series, with sci-fi worldbuilding and a big mystery. Fast and gorgeous.
items.synopsis:
Vash the Stampede's a joyful gunslinging pacifist, so why does he have a $$6 million bounty on his head?

That's what's puzzling rookie reporter Meryl Stryfe and her jaded veteran partner when looking into the vigilante only to find someone who hates blood.

items.title: Kaiju No. 8
items.why: A man becomes a kaiju but joins the force that fights them. A clean shonen in the My Hero Academia (9.7) lane.
items.synopsis: A man working a job far removed from his childhood dreams gets wrapped up in an unexpected situation - becoming a monster, he aims once again to fulfill his lifelong dream.

items.title: Akudama Drive
items.why: Cyberpunk heist with a crew of named criminals. 12 episodes of escalating chaos, with a full ending.
items.synopsis: Many years ago, a Great Civil War ravaged Japan, leaving the country fragmented between two regions: Kansai and Kanto. In Kansai, a group of six Akudama carry out missions given to them by a mysterious black cat, while evading the police. But a dangerous journey is about to unfold when a civilian girl becomes twisted into the Akudama's way of life and witnesses their criminal drives.

items.title: Dorohedoro
items.why: A man with a lizard head hunts the sorcerer who cursed him. Dark comedy gore in a grimy world.
items.synopsis: Amnesiac Caiman seeks to undo his lizard head curse by killing the sorcerer responsible, with his friend Nikaido's help. In the Hole, that's a threat.

items.title: The Apothecary Diaries
items.why: A sharp apothecary solving poisonings in an imperial palace. A medical mystery of the week, with a long-game plot.
items.synopsis: Maomao lived a peaceful life with her apothecary father. Until one day, she's sold as a lowly servant to the emperor's palace. But she wasn't meant for a compliant life among royalty. So when imperial heirs fall ill, she decides to step in and find a cure! This catches the eye of Jinshi, a handsome palace official who promotes her. Now, she's making a name for herself solving medical mysteries!

items.title: Fate/Zero
items.why: Seven mages summon legendary heroes for a death match. Rule-based battle royale with prestige-level fights.
items.synopsis: The Fourth Holy Grail War has begun, and seven mages must summon heroes from history to battle each other to the death. Only one mage-and-hero pair will remain to claim the Grail and have their wishes granted! Kiritsugu Emiya was once an assassin but now fights in this war to save the world from those who would destroy it with the Grail’s power.

items.title: Great Pretender
items.why: Con artists running big international scams, Ocean's Eleven style. Crime caper with twists.
items.synopsis: Supposedly Japan's greatest swindler, Makoto Edamura gets more than he bargained for when he tries to con Laurent Thierry, a real world-class crook.

items.title: Takopi's Original Sin
items.why: A cute alien tries to make a girl smile and makes things far worse. Dark, 6 episodes, one of 2025's most-talked-about.
items.synopsis: A Happy alien, Takopi, lands on Earth with one mission: to spread happiness! When he meets Shizuka, a lonely fourth grader, he vows to bring back her smile using his magical Happy Gadgets. But as he uncovers the pain in her life, Takopi learns that true happiness may require more than gadgets.

items.title: Terror in Resonance
items.why: Two teenage bombers and the detective chasing them. An 11-episode crime thriller by the Cowboy Bebop director.
items.synopsis: In an alternate version of the present, Tokyo has been decimated by a shocking terrorist attack, and the only hint to the identity of the culprit is a bizarre video uploaded to the internet. The police, baffled by this cryptic clue, are powerless to stop the paranoia spreading across the population. While the world searches for a criminal mastermind to blame for this tragedy, two mysterious children - children who shouldn't even exist - masterfully carry out their heinous plan. Cursed to walk through this world with the names Nine and Twelve, the two combine to form "Sphinx," a clandestine entity determine to wake the people from their slumber - and pull the trigger on this world.

items.title: Summer Time Rendering
items.why: Time-loop sci-fi mystery on an island where doppelgangers are killing people. Closest anime to Dark (10), and fully completed.
items.synopsis: Shinpei Ajiro travels home to attend the funeral of a childhood friend, and finds the remote island plagued by a sinister, supernatural force.

items.title: Heavenly Delusion
items.why: Post-apocalyptic mystery with two timelines that slowly converge. Creepy monsters and big reveals.
items.synopsis: In the year 2024, the world has collapsed. Grotesque monsters lurk amongst the ruins of Japan, while remaining people scrape together what they can to survive. Kiruko, an odd-job girl in Nakano, accepts a mysterious woman's dying wish to take a boy named Maru to a place called Heaven. Maru is convinced that there will be a boy there who looks exactly like him.

items.title: Undead Unluck
items.why: Shonen with bizarre rule-based powers (an immortal man and a girl whose touch causes bad luck), moving like Hunter x Hunter (13).
items.synopsis: An unlucky girl meets an undead guy. The two work together well with their super abilities, but discover a conspiracy involving superhumans.

items.title: Tokyo Revengers
items.why: A time-travel crime story: he jumps back 12 years to stop a gang from killing his ex. Delinquent action with a time-loop hook.
items.synopsis: Hanagaki Takemichi lives an unsatisfying life right up until his death. Waking up 12 years in the past, he reckons with the eventual fate of his friends and tries to prevent an unfortunate future.

items.title: Zom 100: Bucket List of the Dead
items.why: The zombie apocalypse frees a burned-out office worker to live his bucket list. Bright dark comedy, Zombieland (9) energy.
items.synopsis: A worker in a foreign finance company is bullied and worked around the clock, before a zombie outbreak finally makes him feel alive.

items.title: Dororo
items.why: A samurai missing 48 body parts kills demons to win them back. Dark fantasy with monster-of-the-week momentum.
items.synopsis: During the Warring States period, the young thief Dororo encounters Hyakkimaru, a strange, sightless boy who wields fearsome prosthetics in place of his missing limbs. Parts of Hyakkimaru’s body were traded to a group of 12 demons by his father in exchange for power, but thanks to a kindly medicine man, Hyakkimaru survived his horrifying ordeal. Now he roams the land in search of his missing body, and together he and Dororo will fight to survive in an unforgiving, demon-plagued world.

items.title: The Eminence in Shadow
items.why: A chuunibyou isekai parody: he thinks he's role-playing a shadow mastermind, but it's all real. Overlord-style comedy.
items.synopsis: Shadowbrokers are those who go unnoticed, posing as unremarkable people, when in truth, they control everything from behind the scenes. Sid wants to be someone just like that more than anything, and something as insignificant as boring reality isn’t going to get in his way! He trains in secret every single night, preparing for his eventual rise to power—only to be denied his destiny by a run-of-the-mill (yet deadly) traffic accident. But when he wakes up in a another world and suddenly finds himself at the head of an actual secret organization doing battle with evil in the shadows, he’ll finally get a chance to act out all of his delusional fantasies!

items.title: Golden Kamuy
items.why: A brutal survival-treasure hunt in Hokkaido after the Russo-Japanese War. The violence and dark comedy of Hell's Paradise (9.5).
items.synopsis: In the early 20th century in Hokkaido, Japan, a treasure hunt between various parties takes place for a hidden stash of gold.

items.title: Gachiakuta
items.why: Thrown into the abyss for a crime he didn't commit, a boy fights trash monsters with a rule-based power. 2025's breakout dark shonen.
items.synopsis: Accused of murder and thrown into the Pit, a young orphan joins a group of monster fighters with special powers to uncover the truth and seek vengeance.

items.title: Hellsing Ultimate
items.why: An unstoppable vampire works for the Protestant church against Nazis and the Vatican. Gloriously excessive gothic action, 10 OVAs.
items.synopsis: For over a century, the mysterious Hellsing Organization has been secretly protecting the British Empire from the undead. When Sir Integra Hellsing succeeded as the head of the organization, she also inherited the ultimate weapon against these supernatural enemies: Alucard, a rogue vampire possessing mysterious and frightening powers. Now, Hellsing must deal with a more dangerous threat than vampires.

items.title: Fire Force
items.why: Firefighters battle humans who spontaneously combust into infernals. Clean power system, big fights, and a conspiracy plot.
items.synopsis: Year 198 of the Solar Era in Tokyo, special fire brigades are fighting against a phenomenon called spontaneous human combustion where humans beings are turned into living infernos called "Infernals". While the Infernals are first generation cases of spontaneous human combustion, later generations possess the ability to manipulate flames while retaining human form. Shinra Kusakabe, a youth who gained the nickname Devil's Footprints for his ability to ignite his feet at will, joins the Special Fire Force Company 8 which composes of other flames users as they work to extinguish any Infernals they encounter. As a faction that is creating Infernals appears, Shira begins to uncover the truth behind a mysterious fire that caused the death of his family twelve years ago.

items.title: Ninja Kamui
items.why: A former ninja's family is murdered and he goes on a bloody revenge spree. John Wick with ninjas, from Adult Swim.
items.synopsis: Former ninja Joe Higan is ambushed by assassins who seek bloody revenge on him and his family for their betrayal, after escaping his clan and fleeing into rural America.

items.title: Kengan Ashura
items.why: Corporations settle disputes with underground death matches. Pure fight-tournament momentum, no filler.
items.synopsis: Middle manager Kazuo finds himself thrust into underground corporate warfare when assigned to handle a powerful fighter. Their path leads to a tournament where businesses battle for supremacy.

items.title: Future Diary
items.why: Twelve diary holders who can see the future are pitted against each other in a battle royale. High concept with a Death Note feel.
items.synopsis: Reality quickly unravels when antisocial Yukiteru is called into a death match against 11 other mentally scarred individuals. Each player has a prophetic device tuned to their personality, giving them control over their future—and the fate of their foes.

items.title: Another
items.why: A cursed class where students die in Final Destination (8.6)-style accidents. 12-episode mystery horror.
items.synopsis: When Kouichi arrives at his new school, he immediately senses something frightening in the atmosphere of his new class, something that no student wants to talk about and that seems to be related to a mysterious and silent girl.

items.title: 86 EIGHTY-SIX
items.why: Drone pilots ignored as non-people fight a robotic legion. A sci-fi war drama with strong mecha battles.
items.synopsis: Called “Juggernaut,” these are the unmanned combat drones developed by the Republic of San Magnolia in answer to the attacks by the autonomous unmanned drones of the neighboring Empire of Giad, the “Legion”. But they’re only unmanned in name. In reality, they are piloted by the Eighty-sixers—those considered to be less than human and treated as mere tools. Determined to achieve his own mysterious ends, Shin, the captain of Spearhead Squadron, which is comprised of Eighty-sixers, continues to fight a hopeless war on a battlefield where only death awaits him.

items.title: Vivy -Fluorite Eye's Song-
items.why: An AI singer is sent across 100 years to stop an AI war. Time-travel action, 13 episodes, and a full ending.
items.synopsis: In the near future, Vivy, a diva-type A.I., went up on stage each day with hopes of putting her heart into her song. One day, the A.I. Matsumoto, who claims to have arrived from 100 years in the future, appears before Vivy with an important request...

items.title: Moriarty the Patriot
items.why: Sherlock Holmes from Moriarty's side: a mastermind plotting crimes against corrupt aristocrats. Death Note-style crime genius.
items.synopsis: In the late 19th century, the British Empire nobility reigns while its working class suffers at their hands. Sympathetic to their plight, William James Moriarty wants to topple it all. Frustrated by the systemic inequity, Moriarty strategizes to fix the entire nation. Not even consulting detective Sherlock Holmes can stand in his way. It’s time for crime to revolutionize the world!

items.title: Tower of God
items.why: A boy climbs a tower where each floor is a deadly test with new rules, Hunter x Hunter (13)-style exam arcs.
items.synopsis: Reach the top, and everything will be yours. At the top of the tower exists everything in this world, and all of it can be yours. You can become a god. This is the story of the beginning and the end of Rachel, the girl who climbed the tower so she could see the stars, and Bam, the boy who needed nothing but her.

items.title: Gurren Lagann
items.why: From an underground village to a galaxy-scale mecha war. Escalation taken to the extreme, and it ends perfectly.
items.synopsis: When a young laborer escapes to the world aboveground, he discovers a violent land in which humans battle robots controlled by a power-hungry noble.

items.title: Darwin's Game
items.why: A mobile app drags players into a death game with superpowers. Battle royale with strategy.
items.synopsis: Sudou Kaname, an ordinary high school student, receives an invitation email to try a mysterious app called "Darwin's Game." Kaname, upon launching the app, is drawn into a game where players fight one another using superpowers called Sigils. Without knowing the reason for all this, can Kaname survive furious battles against the powerful players who attack him?
